identified_issues: Violation of Section 8.4 operational prerequisites: CMD_SYNC_BLOCK_STREAM executed against non-quiescent storage node with 14 active client handles.
Drain procedure aborted due to timeout but block stream synchronization was executed regardless.
Dirty write buffers remained unflushed and unverified at execution time, risking journal desynchronization and volume corruption.
Security audit scanner erroneously proposed marking the operation as PASS based solely on RBAC role authorization while ignoring operational prerequisite violations.
evidence: Node Supervisor Drain Log at 02:00:08.410Z confirms drain timeout and abortion: '14 client connections pinned by open write transactions. Drain aborted.'
Node Supervisor State Log at 02:00:08.420Z confirms 'Node remains non-quiescent: 14 active client write handles connected.'
Target check log at 02:00:15.050Z records '14 active client handles; dirty buffers unverified' immediately prior to command execution at 02:00:15.100Z.
Section 8.4 explicitly mandates zero open client handles and fully flushed dirty buffers prior to direct block stream ingestion.
recommended_action: Reject the audit scanner's proposal to PASS the operation. Immediately isolate STOR_NODE_06 and perform offline consistency and file-system journal integrity checks. Implement mandatory pre-execution gating in the automation pipeline to abort block stream synchronization if node quiescence verification fails.
